issue.title: Desktop resume of a gateway session ignores `model_config.gateway_runtime` and recombines the model with the stale `billing_provider` → 404

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

issue.body:
## Summary

When a session that was last driven by the messaging gateway (Telegram) is resumed in the Desktop app, the Desktop/TUI resume path picks the wrong provider for the stored model. The model name comes from the latest gateway turn, but the provider comes from `sessions.billing_provider`, which records only the route of the session's **first accounted API call** (`hermes_state_usage.py`, `first_accounted_route`). The current gateway route that the gateway already persists in `model_config.gateway_runtime` is never read on this path.

Result: every turn fails with `HTTP 404: model: <model>` because the model is sent to a provider that does not serve it. The user has to switch models manually to recover.

## Root cause (line-level, on current main `bfda74c71ac`)

- The gateway persists the live route per turn: `gateway/run_turn.py` (around L355–379) writes `model_config["gateway_runtime"] = {provider, base_url, api_mode}` plus the `model` column.
- The CLI resume path reads it through the canonical reader: `hermes_cli/cli_model_switch_mixin.py::stored_session_route` → `SessionDB.session_gateway_runtime` (`hermes_state_gateway.py` L776). Its precedence is nested `gateway_runtime` first, then top-level TUI keys, then `billing_provider`.
- The Desktop/TUI resume path does **not** use that reader: `tui_gateway/server.py::_stored_session_runtime_overrides` (L1549–1608) reads only the top-level `model_config.provider`. If that key is absent, it falls back to `billing_provider` (L1572–1575). `gateway_runtime` is ignored.

So a session that started on provider A (billing_provider = A, frozen after the first call) and later ran on provider B through the gateway is resumed on Desktop as `model = <B's model>` + `provider = A`.

## Reproduction (real rows, read-only probe against current main)

I called `tui_gateway.server._stored_session_runtime_overrides` on stored Telegram session rows (read-only DB connection, no writes). Model and provider names are exactly as stored:

| session | gateway last ran (model on `gateway_runtime.provider`) | Desktop resume would pick |
|---|---|---|
| `..._75733a87` | `gpt-6-sol` on `openai-codex` | `gpt-6-sol` on `anthropic` ❌ |
| `..._741587d7` | `gpt-6-sol` on `openai-codex` | `gpt-6-sol` on `anthropic` ❌ |
| `..._578cc1b9` | `claude-opus-5` on `anthropic` | `claude-opus-5` on `openai-codex` ❌ |
| `..._454c9030` | `gpt-6-sol` on `openai-codex` | `gpt-6-sol` on `openai-codex` ✅ (billing_provider happened to match) |

In the ❌ rows the top-level `model_config.provider` is empty. `billing_provider` still holds the first route, while `gateway_runtime.provider` holds the current one.

Observed live (agent.log, profile under a multiplex gateway, Desktop backend):

```
01:10:52 conversation turn: session=..._1fa3f504 model=gpt-6-sol provider=openai-codex platform=telegram
01:15:04 conversation turn: session=..._1fa3f504 model=gpt-6-sol provider=anthropic platform=desktop
01:15:04 Stored system prompt ... has stale runtime identity; rebuilding for model=gpt-6-sol provider=anthropic.
01:15:05 API call failed (attempt 1/3) ... provider=anthropic model=gpt-6-sol summary=HTTP 404: model: gpt-6-sol
01:15:13 API call failed after 3 retries. HTTP 404: model: gpt-6-sol
01:15:46 Model switched in-place: gpt-6-sol (anthropic) -> claude-opus-5-5 (anthropic)   # manual recovery
```

## Expected

Resuming the same session on another surface continues on the route that session last ran on, the same way the CLI already does. The Desktop/TUI path should resolve the provider through `SessionDB.session_gateway_runtime` (or an equivalent that honors `gateway_runtime` before `billing_provider`). It should not fall back to the first-call billing bucket while a newer route is on the row.

## Notes

- #79536 (closed by #85261 / #85977) fixed the provider **not being written** on `/model` switches. This bug is on the **read** side: the route is written (`gateway_runtime`), but the Desktop resume reader does not look at it. Both fixes are present on the tested commit.
- `billing_provider` looks intentionally frozen after the first accounted call (one row, one billing bucket), so it is a poor fallback whenever a newer route exists.
- Environment: macOS, Hermes `0.21.5` @ `bfda74c71ac` (also on `54fb5a4`), multiplex gateway serving 8 profiles, Desktop app with a profile-launched dashboard backend.

comments.body:
<!-- hermes-autotriage -->
<!-- action=triaged-issue issue=125942 sibling-pr=121629 at=2026-09-28T03:22Z -->

Confirmed the root cause on current `main`: `tui_gateway/server.py::_stored_session_runtime_overrides` reads only top-level `model_config.provider` and then falls back to `billing_provider`; it never consults `model_config["gateway_runtime"]`. The gateway does persist the live route there (`gateway/run_turn.py` ~L375-378), and the CLI resume path already honors it through `SessionDB.session_gateway_runtime` — so this is a Desktop/TUI read-side gap, exactly as reported.

Closest in-flight PR: **#121629** (`fix(tui): resume a fallback-served chat on its picked model and provider`) edits this same function, but it only guards the `billing_provider` mispairing — it does not read `gateway_runtime`, so it won't resolve this case (in the failing rows `model == row_model`, so the guarded fallback still picks `billing_provider`). I've left a note on #121629 suggesting it route the provider through `SessionDB.session_gateway_runtime` before the `billing_provider` fallback, which would close both there. Not opening a competing PR on the same function to avoid churn.

issue.body:
## Problem
Part of #125942. A Telegram session with a current `gateway_runtime` route but no top-level provider resumes in Desktop/TUI with its first-call billing provider. The current model and that old provider are incompatible.

## Root cause
`_stored_session_runtime_overrides` ignores the nested gateway route. The gateway writer and CLI reader already agree on it; the Desktop reader falls straight from an absent top-level provider to `billing_provider`.

## Change
For non-fallback gateway snapshots without an explicit top-level provider, restore provider, endpoint and wire mode together using `SessionDB.session_gateway_runtime`. Retain existing endpoint validation, custom-provider healing, profile-following exemptions and reasoning/tier handling.

## Verification
Base: `9a0a1625367242596d338ae2da541c4a1fc785a2`.
- RED: real temporary SessionDB, first-call accounting, actual `GatewayTurnMixin._sync_session_model_from_agent`, then CLI/Desktop readers. CLI returned `openai-codex`; Desktop returned stale `anthropic` (1 assertion failure).
- GREEN: `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tui_gateway/test_resume_gateway_runtime.py tests/tui_gateway/test_resume_switched_provider_endpoint.py -q --tb=short -j 1`: **15 passed** on native Windows.
- Includes malformed/empty metadata, incomplete and temporary-fallback snapshots, explicit Desktop selection, endpoint consistency, settings and profile-following exemptions.
- Temporary HOME/USERPROFILE/HERMES_HOME/APPDATA/LOCALAPPDATA; no credentials, live provider calls, installs or service changes.
- Post-publication: 4 selected existing Desktop resume/override tests and all 24 CLI resume tests passed (canonical runner). Together with the 15 focused tests: 43 passed across completed runs.
- The full `test_tui_gateway_server.py` broad run exceeded the 240-second local budget; its worker tree was stopped. That run is unresolved, not PASS. No live GUI/provider request was attempted.
- Independent exact-head Codex CLI review completed with STATIC PASS (read-only, not execution). Official Claude Code 2.1.280 / Opus 5.5 returned HTTP 503 and exited 1; that review remains blocked, not PASS.

## Non-goals / remaining acceptance
This is deliberately `Part of`, not `Fixes`: rows containing both an explicit Desktop provider and a conflicting gateway snapshot retain existing precedence; temporary fallback-versus-primary resume policy is unchanged. These are distinct policy/ownership contracts, not reasons to keep the reported nested-only row broken.

Overlap inspected: #121629 repairs first-fallback billing model versus picked model, but never reads nested-only gateway routes; #103531 propagates overrides through lazy/deferred builds; #86274 changes writer ordering for fallback versus explicit switches, not restoration of already-persisted nested-only rows. No schema, billing-accounting or write-path changes here.


### Follow-up verification (same head)

- Canonical runner: `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tui_gateway/test_tui_gateway_server.py -k "resume or stored_session_runtime or model_override or provider_override" -vv --tb=short --file-timeout 150 -j 1` — **30 passed**, exit 0, on native Windows with isolated temporary home/config.
- The full server file is still **not verified**: bounded retries stalled near the personality/compression test boundary; excluding compression tests also timed out. These are incomplete runs, not passing coverage and not yet established as baseline failures. Claude Code review remains blocked by the previously reported HTTP 503; Codex static review is unchanged.


### Verification follow-up (2026-09-28, same head `7219cf6b88fdc67c9d38e5c74f2bfcee36a8d052`)

The broader Windows run now completed rather than timing out:

```text
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tui_gateway/test_tui_gateway_server.py -k "not compress" -vv --tb=short --file-timeout 600 -j 1
629 passed, 2 failed, 23 deselected; exit 1
```

Both failures were then reproduced on the frozen base `9a0a1625367242596d338ae2da541c4a1fc785a2`, using the canonical runner and fresh isolated homes:
- `test_profile_scoped_agent_build_starts_mcp_discovery_in_profile_home`: `agent_ready` not set within five seconds on base and the broad head run; passes when selected separately on the head (timing-sensitive, not declared fixed).
- `test_load_cfg_raw_sees_replacement_with_pinned_mtime_and_size`: expected `aaaa-route`, got cached `bbbb-route`, on both base and head.

This is **not a full-suite PASS**: the two baseline failures remain, and the Claude Code review is still unresolved after the previously reported service error. The previously excluded compression selection has now completed separately on the same head, with fresh isolated homes: `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tui_gateway/test_tui_gateway_server.py -k "compress" -vv --tb=short --file-timeout 600 -j 1` — **23 passed, 0 failed; exit 0** (22.9 seconds). The prior focused regression/CLI-resume checks and exact-head Codex static review remain unchanged. No live GUI/provider verification is claimed.

issue.title: fix(tui): resume a fallback-served chat on its picked model and provider

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

repository.name: hermes-agent
repository.description: The agent that grows with you

issue.body: ## What does this PR do? A chat whose **first** successful call was served by a configured fallback provider is rebuilt from `state.db` with the wrong pair: the fallback's **model** on the primary's **provider**. A rebuild happens after an app restart, a Desktop auto-update, an idle reap, an LRU eviction or a backend crash. Reattaching to a chat that is still live is not affected. This isn't only a display problem: - The Desktop model picker shows the fallback model checked under the primary provider's group, a pairing nobody configured. - The next turn really sends the fallback model to the primary provider. That call fails, and the fallback chain then "falls back" from model X to the same model X. **Root cause.** Two writes are each correct on their own, but together they produce a bad read: 1. `hermes_state_usage.py::update_token_counts` (`first_accounted_route`, from `d14006ead2`) rewrites `sessions.model` / `billing_provider` to the route that served the first accounted call. That's right for billing and telemetry, and it leaves `model_config` alone. 2. `tui_gateway/server.py::_stored_session_runtime_overrides` took the model from the row (`row.model or model_config.model`) and the provider from `model_config.provider`. So it combined the fallback model with the primary provider. **Fix.** `model_config` always holds the chat's pick as a consistent model and provider. Resume now reads the model from `model_config` when it has one, and uses the `sessions.model` column only for older rows without it. `billing_provider` is used only when the resolved model equals the column's model, so the billing provider is never paired with a different model. `sessions.model` and `billing_*` stay the billing record, and `d14006ead2`'s behaviour is unchanged. Mid-chat switches still resume correctly, because every writer that saves one updates `model_config.model` together with the column: - TUI/Desktop `model.switch`: `_persist_live_session_runtime` → `_runtime_model_config`. - CLI `/model`: `update_session_model` + `patch_session_model_config`. - Gateway `/model`: `update_session_model(provider=…)`. ## Related Issue Fixes the resume half of #118969. That issue also asks the chat picker to hide non-chat models (for example image models); this PR doesn't do that, so it shouldn't close the issue. - #110279: same symptom written by a different writer (the gateway's `_sync_session_model_from_agent`, with `gateway_runtime.fallback_active`). This fix also restores that issue's stored row as a consistent pair (`glm-5.3` + `zai`), because it changes the reader instead of one writer. - #121506: argues a resumed chat should go back to the primary instead of staying on the fallback. This PR agrees for the TUI/Desktop reader but does not close it: the CLI `--resume` reader is unchanged. - Alternative fixes for the same bug: #118982 (write side: copies the fallback route into `model_config`) and #110282 (same function: restores the fallback pair when `fallback_active` is set). Both resume on the fallback; this PR resumes on the pick. See Reviewers. - Complementary: #121533 (saves the requested route across fallback turns, on the write side). It prevents new bad rows; this PR repairs rows that are already mixed when they are read. Both touch `tui_gateway/server.py`, so whichever lands second rebases and keeps both invariants. (#121540 was closed in favour of #121533.) Also seen in a real Desktop session: the primary failed on the first turn, the fallback answered, Desktop auto-updated, and the next turn logged `model= provider=`. ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) ## Changes Made - `tui_gateway/server.py`: `_stored_session_runtime_overrides` takes the model and provider from one source. - `tests/tui_gateway/test_tui_gateway_server.py`: seam test, parametrized over a picked pair and over a picked model with no provider. The fallback route in the row must never be mixed with the pick. - `tests/tui_gateway/test_resume_switched_provider_endpoint.py`: runs through a real `SessionDB`. It creates the row with the pick, runs `update_token_counts` with the fallback route, and checks two things: the billing columns hold the fallback, and resume restores the picked pair. **Not modified:** `hermes_state_usage.py` (`first_accounted_route` keeps writing the serving route to the billing columns), the session writers, and every existing exemption in `_stored_session_runtime_overrides` (room plumbing, Bot Chat / `composer_override_profile`, foreign-endpoint drop, stale-provider healing, `_BARE_BILLING_PROVIDERS`). **Does not fix:** the CLI `hermes --resume` reader (`stored_session_route`), which still takes the model from the column. See Reviewers. **Known limitation:** a chat with no stored provider (`model_config = {model: M}`) whose first call a fallback served under the same model id `M` still resumes on the fallback's provider, exactly as on `main`. That row is identical to the stale-provider-healing row pinned by `test_resume_overrides_get_no_stale_provider` (`9ddc6fb23a`), where `billing_provider` stands in for the profile default, so the reader cannot tell them apart. The write side (#121533, recording the requested route) is where this becomes distinguishable. ## Reproduction **Before the fix, in the Desktop app.** Setup: Provider A is the primary and always returns 503, Provider B is the fallback, and a Desktop chat is picked on Provider A. Send one message, which Provider B answers. Quit and relaunch the app, then reopen the chat. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d602cd81-170f-42bc-823f-b6204b6514be The picker shows the fallback **Model B** checked under **Provider A (primary)**, and the Provider B group is gone: **Before and after, end to end without the UI.** This uses the real `_make_agent`, `AIAgent.run_conversation`, `SessionDB`, `_persist_live_session_runtime` and resume, against two local OpenAI-compatible mocks: prov-a always returns 503, prov-b answers. It ran in a throwaway `HERMES_HOME` with the provider credential env vars unset. | | Resumed model + provider | Turn 2 requests | |---|---|---| | Before | `model-b` + `custom:prov-a` | prov-a/**model-b** ×2, then prov-b | | After | `model-a` + `custom:prov-a` | prov-a/model-a (retried), then prov-b/model-b (normal fallback) | In both runs the stored row keeps `model=model-b`, `billing_provider=prov-b`, so the billing record is unchanged. ## How to Test 1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tui_gateway/test_resume_switched_provider_endpoint.py tests/tui_gateway/test_tui_gateway_server.py -k "fallback_served_first_call or never_pairs_billing_model"`: all 3 cases are red on `main` and green on this branch. 2. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tui_gateway/test_tui_gateway_server.py tests/tui_gateway/test_resume_*.py tests/hermes_cli/test_resume_model_restore.py tests/hermes_state/`: 2036 passed, 4 failed (after rebasing onto current `main`). The same 4 fail on `main` without this change (3 × `test_cross_vm_fs_wal_refusal`, `test_guest_durability_barriers`; macOS environment tests). 3. Manual: configure a primary that fails plus a fallback, pick the primary in a Desktop chat, send one message, restart the app and reopen the chat. The picker shows the primary pair, and the next turn tries the primary model on the primary provider before falling back. ## Reviewers - **Which consistent pair should a resumed chat get: the pick or the fallback?** All the open fixes stop the mismatched pair; they differ on this. This PR resumes on the user's pick, because: - fallback is turn-scoped by design: `restore_primary_runtime` (`agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py`) runs at the start of every turn so a live chat retries the primary. Resuming on the pick gives a rebuilt chat the same behaviour; - resuming on the fallback makes it the rebuilt agent's primary, so the chat never returns to the primary even after it recovers (#121506); - `sessions.model` / `billing_*` stay the record of what served the call, and `model_config` stays the record of the pick. The cost: if the primary is still broken, the first turn after each resume fails once before falling back. For a pick that can never work (the image model in #118969), that happens on every resume until the user re-picks. #118982 avoids it. If you prefer the resume-on-fallback design, #118982 / #110282 are the way to go and this PR can be closed. - **Rows written before `56a41715dc` (2026-08-14).** On those builds, a CLI or gateway `/model` switch updated the model column but not `model_config.model`. If such a switch happened on a Desktop or TUI row, the chat now resumes on the model that was picked before the switch, with its matching provider. Before, it resumed on a mismatched pair. Is that acceptable for those old rows? - **Picked model with no stored provider.** If the model column holds a different model, the chat now resumes on the picked model with the configured default provider, instead of the fallback route. - **api_server browser lock.** `update_session_runtime_lock` writes the model column but not `model_config.model`. If a row that has a Desktop pick is later locked to another model through api_server, Desktop resume restores the Desktop pick. Before, that case produced a mismatched pair. - **Out of scope: the CLI `hermes --resume` path.** `stored_session_route` in `hermes_cli/cli_model_switch_mixin.py` has a related version of this bug. It takes the model from the column and the provider from `session_gateway_runtime`, so a Desktop row resumed from the CLI would still get the mismatched pair. I plan to fix it in a separate PR unless you'd rather it land here. ## Checklist ### Code - [x] I've read the Contributing Guide - [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits - [x] I searched for existing PRs to make sure this isn't a duplicate - [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix - [x] Tests run with `scripts/run_tests.sh` (see How to Test; 5 failures on `main` are unrelated) - [x] I've added tests for my changes - [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS 26.6 ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [x] Documentation: N/A - [x] `cli-config.yaml.example`: N/A - [x] `CONTRIBUTING.md` / `AGENTS.md`: N/A - [x] Cross-platform impact: N/A --- Model and harness: Claude Opus 5.5 via Hermes Agent.

issue.body:
Desktop/TUI surfaces served by one pooled backend now act on the profile that OWNS the session or the rail selection instead of the backend's launch profile: `/save`, the interrupt hook, `/model` live sync, the exit resume hint, gateway-session resume, the new-chat slash palette, the error card's Open Logs, and the API-server card.

## Per issue

- Fixes #125241 — `tui_gateway/methods_session.py` `session.save` built `saved_dir` from `get_hermes_home()` (launch profile); it now uses the session's `profile_home` like `session.history`/`session.create`. Salvages #125242 by @jonpol01.
- Fixes #125063 — `tui_gateway/session_lifecycle.py::_interrupt_session_turn` dispatched `agent_loop_stopped` with no profile runtime scope; the dispatch is now inside `_session_profile_runtime_scope(session, hydrate_secrets=False)`, which covers every caller (`session.interrupt`, WS orphan reaper, idle reaper, lease takeover, compute-host close). Salvages #125073 by @dskwe (earliest; #125081 by @kokhlo is the same wrap → duplicate).
- Fixes #122655 — `tui_gateway/methods_slash.py::_mirror_slash_side_effects` ran `/model`'s `switch_model → resolve_runtime` credential read off-turn with no scope bound → `UnscopedSecretError` under multiplex; the mirror dispatch is wrapped in `_session_profile_runtime_scope(session)`. Salvages #122698 by @ahisblessed. (#125038 is a different bug — curator thread contextvars, #125032 — not salvaged here.)
- Fixes #125078 — `hermes_cli/main_tui_launch.py::_print_tui_exit_summary` now appends `-p <profile>` for non-`default`/`custom` profiles, matching `cli_session_mixin.py::_print_exit_summary`. Salvages #125079 by @dskwe.
- Fixes #125942 — `tui_gateway/server.py::_stored_session_runtime_overrides` read only top-level `model_config.provider` then `billing_provider`, ignoring the `gateway_runtime` route `gateway/run_turn.py` persists; it now uses the canonical `SessionDB.session_gateway_runtime` reader (nested `gateway_runtime` → top-level TUI keys, with a routable `billing_provider` filling a missing provider) that CLI `--resume` already uses. **CLI-visible precedence change:** a TUI-written row with top-level `base_url`/`api_mode` and no `provider` used to restore the endpoint alone (ambient provider); it now also restores the `billing_provider` that served it — the merge `tui_gateway/server.py` always did, now shared by `cli_model_switch_mixin.py::stored_session_route` (bare `auto`/`custom` buckets still contribute nothing). Slim redo of #125956 by @Wenfengcheng (its second reader inverted the precedence). #123799 and #121629 do not fix this.
- Fixes #124651 — Desktop `use-slash-completions.ts` sent `commands.catalog`/`complete.slash` with empty params for a draft, so `tui_gateway/methods_tools.py::_session_home_scope` scanned the launch home; the hook now passes the rail-selected `profile` when there is no `session_id`, and `commands.catalog`/`complete.slash`/`skills.reload` accept `profile` (contracts regenerated). Salvages #124845 by @chelsealong.
- Fixes #119080 — `apps/desktop/electron/fs-ipc.ts` `hermes:fs:logsRoot` resolved `readActiveDesktopProfile()`; the IPC now takes the owning profile and the error card passes the composer scope's profile (`default` → the home's own `logs/`). Sibling symptom (secondary-profile `gui.log` landing in the launch home) is a backend logging mechanism (`hermes_logging.py::_ProfileRoutingFileHandler`), tracked separately — not claimed here.
- Fixes #121125 — `hermes_cli/web_routers/messaging.py::_messaging_platform_payload` reported a served secondary's API server as disabled/needs-setup from its own never-configured config; a live `mirrored_from` entry from `gateway/status.py::shared_listener_mirror_platforms` now projects enabled+configured. Salvages #122165 by @Finn763.

## Cells (WHEN × WHERE)

L6 (RPC methods) and L2 (session end / interrupt hook) on T7 (Desktop pooled `serve`, several homes per process) and T2/T3 (multiplex gateway, default- or named-hosted). #125078 is the T1/T3 CLI entry-point twin of an already-fixed CLI path; #125942 is the T7 read path diverging from the canonical CLI reader.

## Validation

| Item | Test | Red on base (origin/main) | Green on head |
|---|---|---|---|
| #125241 | `tests/tui_gateway/test_tui_gateway_server.py::test_session_save_lands_in_the_sessions_own_profile_a_b_a` | index 1 was `.hermes/sessions/saved`, expected `profiles/s6probe-work/sessions/saved` (A→B→A, `set_multiplex_active(True)`) | pass |

pull_request.title: fix(tui): resume a fallback-served chat on its picked model and provider
pull_request.body: ## What does this PR do? A chat whose **first** successful call was served by a configured fallback provider is rebuilt from `state.db` with the wrong pair: the fallback's **model** on the primary's **provider**. A rebuild happens after an app restart, a Desktop auto-update, an idle reap, an LRU eviction or a backend crash. Reattaching to a chat that is still live is not affected. This isn't only a display problem: - The Desktop model picker shows the fallback model checked under the primary provider's group, a pairing nobody configured. - The next turn really sends the fallback model to the primary provider. That call fails, and the fallback chain then "falls back" from model X to the same model X. **Root cause.** Two writes are each correct on their own, but together they produce a bad read: 1. `hermes_state_usage.py::update_token_counts` (`first_accounted_route`, from `d14006ead2`) rewrites `sessions.model` / `billing_provider` to the route that served the first accounted call. That's right for billing and telemetry, and it leaves `model_config` alone. 2. `tui_gateway/server.py::_stored_session_runtime_overrides` took the model from the row (`row.model or model_config.model`) and the provider from `model_config.provider`. So it combined the fallback model with the primary provider. **Fix.** `model_config` always holds the chat's pick as a consistent model and provider. Resume now reads the model from `model_config` when it has one, and uses the `sessions.model` column only for older rows without it. `billing_provider` is used only when the resolved model equals the column's model, so the billing provider is never paired with a different model. `sessions.model` and `billing_*` stay the billing record, and `d14006ead2`'s behaviour is unchanged. Mid-chat switches still resume correctly, because every writer that saves one updates `model_config.model` together with the column: - TUI/Desktop `model.switch`: `_persist_live_session_runtime` → `_runtime_model_config`. - CLI `/model`: `update_session_model` + `patch_session_model_config`. - Gateway `/model`: `update_session_model(provider=…)`. ## Related Issue Fixes the resume half of #118969. That issue also asks the chat picker to hide non-chat models (for example image models); this PR doesn't do that, so it shouldn't close the issue. - #110279: same symptom written by a different writer (the gateway's `_sync_session_model_from_agent`, with `gateway_runtime.fallback_active`). This fix also restores that issue's stored row as a consistent pair (`glm-5.3` + `zai`), because it changes the reader instead of one writer. - #121506: argues a resumed chat should go back to the primary instead of staying on the fallback. This PR agrees for the TUI/Desktop reader but does not close it: the CLI `--resume` reader is unchanged. - Alternative fixes for the same bug: #118982 (write side: copies the fallback route into `model_config`) and #110282 (same function: restores the fallback pair when `fallback_active` is set). Both resume on the fallback; this PR resumes on the pick. See Reviewers. - Complementary: #121533 (saves the requested route across fallback turns, on the write side). It prevents new bad rows; this PR repairs rows that are already mixed when they are read. Both touch `tui_gateway/server.py`, so whichever lands second rebases and keeps both invariants. (#121540 was closed in favour of #121533.) Also seen in a real Desktop session: the primary failed on the first turn, the fallback answered, Desktop auto-updated, and the next turn logged `model= provider=`. ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) ## Changes Made - `tui_gateway/server.py`: `_stored_session_runtime_overrides` takes the model and provider from one source. - `tests/tui_gateway/test_tui_gateway_server.py`: seam test, parametrized over a picked pair and over a picked model with no provider. The fallback route in the row must never be mixed with the pick. - `tests/tui_gateway/test_resume_switched_provider_endpoint.py`: runs through a real `SessionDB`. It creates the row with the pick, runs `update_token_counts` with the fallback route, and checks two things: the billing columns hold the fallback, and resume restores the picked pair. **Not modified:** `hermes_state_usage.py` (`first_accounted_route` keeps writing the serving route to the billing columns), the session writers, and every existing exemption in `_stored_session_runtime_overrides` (room plumbing, Bot Chat / `composer_override_profile`, foreign-endpoint drop, stale-provider healing, `_BARE_BILLING_PROVIDERS`). **Does not fix:** the CLI `hermes --resume` reader (`stored_session_route`), which still takes the model from the column. See Reviewers. **Known limitation:** a chat with no stored provider (`model_config = {model: M}`) whose first call a fallback served under the same model id `M` still resumes on the fallback's provider, exactly as on `main`. That row is identical to the stale-provider-healing row pinned by `test_resume_overrides_get_no_stale_provider` (`9ddc6fb23a`), where `billing_provider` stands in for the profile default, so the reader cannot tell them apart. The write side (#121533, recording the requested route) is where this becomes distinguishable. ## Reproduction **Before the fix, in the Desktop app.** Setup: Provider A is the primary and always returns 503, Provider B is the fallback, and a Desktop chat is picked on Provider A. Send one message, which Provider B answers. Quit and relaunch the app, then reopen the chat. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d602cd81-170f-42bc-823f-b6204b6514be The picker shows the fallback **Model B** checked under **Provider A (primary)**, and the Provider B group is gone: **Before and after, end to end without the UI.** This uses the real `_make_agent`, `AIAgent.run_conversation`, `SessionDB`, `_persist_live_session_runtime` and resume, against two local OpenAI-compatible mocks: prov-a always returns 503, prov-b answers. It ran in a throwaway `HERMES_HOME` with the provider credential env vars unset. | | Resumed model + provider | Turn 2 requests | |---|---|---| | Before | `model-b` + `custom:prov-a` | prov-a/**model-b** ×2, then prov-b | | After | `model-a` + `custom:prov-a` | prov-a/model-a (retried), then prov-b/model-b (normal fallback) | In both runs the stored row keeps `model=model-b`, `billing_provider=prov-b`, so the billing record is unchanged. ## How to Test 1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tui_gateway/test_resume_switched_provider_endpoint.py tests/tui_gateway/test_tui_gateway_server.py -k "fallback_served_first_call or never_pairs_billing_model"`: all 3 cases are red on `main` and green on this branch. 2. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tui_gateway/test_tui_gateway_server.py tests/tui_gateway/test_resume_*.py tests/hermes_cli/test_resume_model_restore.py tests/hermes_state/`: 2036 passed, 4 failed (after rebasing onto current `main`). The same 4 fail on `main` without this change (3 × `test_cross_vm_fs_wal_refusal`, `test_guest_durability_barriers`; macOS environment tests). 3. Manual: configure a primary that fails plus a fallback, pick the primary in a Desktop chat, send one message, restart the app and reopen the chat. The picker shows the primary pair, and the next turn tries the primary model on the primary provider before falling back. ## Reviewers - **Which consistent pair should a resumed chat get: the pick or the fallback?** All the open fixes stop the mismatched pair; they differ on this. This PR resumes on the user's pick, because: - fallback is turn-scoped by design: `restore_primary_runtime` (`agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py`) runs at the start of every turn so a live chat retries the primary. Resuming on the pick gives a rebuilt chat the same behaviour; - resuming on the fallback makes it the rebuilt agent's primary, so the chat never returns to the primary even after it recovers (#121506); - `sessions.model` / `billing_*` stay the record of what served the call, and `model_config` stays the record of the pick. The cost: if the primary is still broken, the first turn after each resume fails once before falling back. For a pick that can never work (the image model in #118969), that happens on every resume until the user re-picks. #118982 avoids it. If you prefer the resume-on-fallback design, #118982 / #110282 are the way to go and this PR can be closed. - **Rows written before `56a41715dc` (2026-08-14).** On those builds, a CLI or gateway `/model` switch updated the model column but not `model_config.model`. If such a switch happened on a Desktop or TUI row, the chat now resumes on the model that was picked before the switch, with its matching provider. Before, it resumed on a mismatched pair. Is that acceptable for those old rows? - **Picked model with no stored provider.** If the model column holds a different model, the chat now resumes on the picked model with the configured default provider, instead of the fallback route. - **api_server browser lock.** `update_session_runtime_lock` writes the model column but not `model_config.model`. If a row that has a Desktop pick is later locked to another model through api_server, Desktop resume restores the Desktop pick. Before, that case produced a mismatched pair. - **Out of scope: the CLI `hermes --resume` path.** `stored_session_route` in `hermes_cli/cli_model_switch_mixin.py` has a related version of this bug. It takes the model from the column and the provider from `session_gateway_runtime`, so a Desktop row resumed from the CLI would still get the mismatched pair. I plan to fix it in a separate PR unless you'd rather it land here. ## Checklist ### Code - [x] I've read the Contributing Guide - [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits - [x] I searched for existing PRs to make sure this isn't a duplicate - [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix - [x] Tests run with `scripts/run_tests.sh` (see How to Test; 5 failures on `main` are unrelated) - [x] I've added tests for my changes - [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS 26.6 ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [x] Documentation: N/A - [x] `cli-config.yaml.example`: N/A - [x] `CONTRIBUTING.md` / `AGENTS.md`: N/A - [x] Cross-platform impact: N/A --- Model and harness: Claude Opus 5.5 via Hermes Agent.

commit.message:
fix(tui): resume a fallback-served chat on its picked model and provider

When the first accounted call of a chat is served by a fallback provider,
update_token_counts (first_accounted_route, d14006ead2) rewrites
sessions.model / billing_* to the serving route but leaves model_config,
which holds the user's pick. _stored_session_runtime_overrides took the
model from the column and the provider from model_config, so a chat
rebuilt from state.db (restart, update, reap) ran the fallback model on
the primary provider.

Read the model from model_config when it has one and fall back to the
column only for older rows; only use billing_provider when the model
also came from the column. sessions.model stays the billing record.
Mid-chat switch writers (model.switch, CLI and gateway /model) already
update model_config.model with the column.

Refs #118969 (resume half)
Refs #110279, #121506

pull_request.title: fix(tui): restore gateway-only runtime route on resume
pull_request.body:
## Problem
Part of #125942. A Telegram session with a current `gateway_runtime` route but no top-level provider resumes in Desktop/TUI with its first-call billing provider. The current model and that old provider are incompatible.

## Root cause
`_stored_session_runtime_overrides` ignores the nested gateway route. The gateway writer and CLI reader already agree on it; the Desktop reader falls straight from an absent top-level provider to `billing_provider`.

## Change
For non-fallback gateway snapshots without an explicit top-level provider, restore provider, endpoint and wire mode together using `SessionDB.session_gateway_runtime`. Retain existing endpoint validation, custom-provider healing, profile-following exemptions and reasoning/tier handling.

## Verification
Base: `9a0a1625367242596d338ae2da541c4a1fc785a2`.
- RED: real temporary SessionDB, first-call accounting, actual `GatewayTurnMixin._sync_session_model_from_agent`, then CLI/Desktop readers. CLI returned `openai-codex`; Desktop returned stale `anthropic` (1 assertion failure).
- GREEN: `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tui_gateway/test_resume_gateway_runtime.py tests/tui_gateway/test_resume_switched_provider_endpoint.py -q --tb=short -j 1`: **15 passed** on native Windows.
- Includes malformed/empty metadata, incomplete and temporary-fallback snapshots, explicit Desktop selection, endpoint consistency, settings and profile-following exemptions.
- Temporary HOME/USERPROFILE/HERMES_HOME/APPDATA/LOCALAPPDATA; no credentials, live provider calls, installs or service changes.
- Post-publication: 4 selected existing Desktop resume/override tests and all 24 CLI resume tests passed (canonical runner). Together with the 15 focused tests: 43 passed across completed runs.
- The full `test_tui_gateway_server.py` broad run exceeded the 240-second local budget; its worker tree was stopped. That run is unresolved, not PASS. No live GUI/provider request was attempted.
- Independent exact-head Codex CLI review completed with STATIC PASS (read-only, not execution). Official Claude Code 2.1.280 / Opus 5.5 returned HTTP 503 and exited 1; that review remains blocked, not PASS.

## Non-goals / remaining acceptance
This is deliberately `Part of`, not `Fixes`: rows containing both an explicit Desktop provider and a conflicting gateway snapshot retain existing precedence; temporary fallback-versus-primary resume policy is unchanged. These are distinct policy/ownership contracts, not reasons to keep the reported nested-only row broken.

Overlap inspected: #121629 repairs first-fallback billing model versus picked model, but never reads nested-only gateway routes; #103531 propagates overrides through lazy/deferred builds; #86274 changes writer ordering for fallback versus explicit switches, not restoration of already-persisted nested-only rows. No schema, billing-accounting or write-path changes here.


### Follow-up verification (same head)

- Canonical runner: `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tui_gateway/test_tui_gateway_server.py -k "resume or stored_session_runtime or model_override or provider_override" -vv --tb=short --file-timeout 150 -j 1` — **30 passed**, exit 0, on native Windows with isolated temporary home/config.
- The full server file is still **not verified**: bounded retries stalled near the personality/compression test boundary; excluding compression tests also timed out. These are incomplete runs, not passing coverage and not yet established as baseline failures. Claude Code review remains blocked by the previously reported HTTP 503; Codex static review is unchanged.


### Verification follow-up (2026-09-28, same head `7219cf6b88fdc67c9d38e5c74f2bfcee36a8d052`)

The broader Windows run now completed rather than timing out:

```text
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tui_gateway/test_tui_gateway_server.py -k "not compress" -vv --tb=short --file-timeout 600 -j 1
629 passed, 2 failed, 23 deselected; exit 1
```

Both failures were then reproduced on the frozen base `9a0a1625367242596d338ae2da541c4a1fc785a2`, using the canonical runner and fresh isolated homes:
- `test_profile_scoped_agent_build_starts_mcp_discovery_in_profile_home`: `agent_ready` not set within five seconds on base and the broad head run; passes when selected separately on the head (timing-sensitive, not declared fixed).
- `test_load_cfg_raw_sees_replacement_with_pinned_mtime_and_size`: expected `aaaa-route`, got cached `bbbb-route`, on both base and head.

This is **not a full-suite PASS**: the two baseline failures remain, and the Claude Code review is still unresolved after the previously reported service error. The previously excluded compression selection has now completed separately on the same head, with fresh isolated homes: `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tui_gateway/test_tui_gateway_server.py -k "compress" -vv --tb=short --file-timeout 600 -j 1` — **23 passed, 0 failed; exit 0** (22.9 seconds). The prior focused regression/CLI-resume checks and exact-head Codex static review remain unchanged. No live GUI/provider verification is claimed.

+"""Resume a gateway-written route without borrowing the first billing provider."""

+from gateway.run_turn import GatewayTurnMixin

+    config = load_config()
+    assert resolve_provider_full("anthropic", config.get("providers")) is not None
+    assert resolve_provider_full("openai-codex", config.get("providers")) is not None
